title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
summary: Return the median of all entries from both sorted arrays, keeping duplicates.

contractDetails.constraints: Each array contains 0–1,000 nondecreasing integers in [−1,000,000, 1,000,000]. At least one array is nonempty. The result is checked as a finite number and is exact for integers and halves.
contractDetails.output-checking: Exact finite numeric equality. Integer and decimal representations of the same value are accepted.

statement: Return the median of all entries from both sorted arrays, keeping duplicates. For an odd total, return the middle entry. For an even total, return the arithmetic mean of the two middle entries. Return a numeric result and use logarithmic time.

examples.explanation: The third value in sorted order is 1.
The two middle values are 1 and 4.
With one array empty, average the other array's two values.

constraints: Each array contains 0–1,000 nondecreasing integers in [−1,000,000, 1,000,000]. At least one array is nonempty. The result is checked as a finite number and is exact for integers and halves.
hints: Conceptual: Split the combined values into a lower half and an upper half without merging the arrays.
Directional: Binary-search how many values the shorter array contributes to the lower half. The total lower-half size determines the other cut.
Implementation: Compare each left boundary with the opposite right boundary. At a valid partition, use the largest left value and, for an even total, the smallest right value.
complexityAnalysis: O(log(min(m,n)+1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space. The search moves only the shorter array's partition.
